The paper considers the problem of electromagnetic radiation and scattering from perfectly conducting bodies of revolution of arbitrary shape.
The mathematical formulation is an integro-differential equation obtained from the potential integrals and boundary conditions.
The method of moments is used to reduce the functional problem to a finite dimensional matrix problem.
The Fourier series expansion in the azimuthal angle decouples the problem into a set of independent modes.
The current is expanded using harmonic functions in the azimuthal angle and subsectional triangle functions in the contour length variable.
The impedance matrix elements are computed using numerical integration techniques with piecewise pulse function approximations.
The radiation field is computed as a linear functional of the current using the measurement matrix approach.
Computations are demonstrated for a conducting sphere and a cone-sphere geometry.
The results for the sphere show good agreement between the general program and the classical eigenfunction solution.
The cone-sphere computations illustrate the application of the matrix method to problems not solvable by classical methods.
The matrix method allows efficient computation of generalized network parameters for arbitrary bodies of revolution.
The flexibility of the matrix approach enables handling a wide range of electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems.
The paper includes a computer program for computing the generalized impedance matrix of an arbitrary body of revolution.
The expansion functions chosen are harmonic in the azimuthal angle and subsectional in the contour length variable.
The use of triangle functions for the contour length expansion provides a piecewise-linear current approximation.
